claims.text: Thermodynamic stability governs whether a stable, coherent protective oxide layer forms and persists on CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Kinetic factors governing oxide formation influence whether the protective layer remains stable.
Controlled additions of Si, Mn, or Al can optimize oxide-layer formation and stability in CrFeCoNi-based alloys.
An optimized X-element composition will improve oxide-layer stability relative to CrFeCoNi without X.
An optimized X-element composition will reduce oxide cracking or spallation relative to CrFeCoNi without X.
The proposed behavior applies to single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution CrFeCoNiX alloys.
The proposed behavior applies in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres at temperatures from 900 to 1200 °C and exposure durations up to 100 hours.
CrFeCoNi without an X-element addition is the defined comparison baseline.
Unstable oxide formation or significant cracking or spallation in the optimized alloy under the specified conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
